llmAnalysis.analysisSummary: The algorithm initializes max_so_far and curr_max to 0, which incorrectly returns 0 for arrays containing only negative numbers. The fix is to start both variables with the first element and iterate from the second element.
llmAnalysis.fixExplanation: The original code set both max_so_far and curr_max to 0, which makes the algorithm return 0 for an all‑negative array. By initializing them with the first array element we correctly capture the maximum possible sum even when all numbers are negative. The loop then starts at index 1, and the standard Kadane update (curr_max = max(arr[i], curr_max + arr[i])) ensures proper handling of each element.
edgeCasesMissed: Empty input array (n == 0) – the current fix assumes at least one element; handling this case would require an early return or guard.
Very large input causing integer overflow – using long long would be safer for large sums.

llmAnalysis.analysisSummary: The binary search implementation has three classic defects: (1) midpoint calculation can overflow, (2) the right bound is initialized one past the last valid index, and (3) when the target is smaller than the middle element the code sets r = mid, which never shrinks the search interval and causes an infinite loop.
llmAnalysis.fixExplanation: Replaced the unsafe midpoint formula with the overflow‑free version, corrected the initial right bound to the last valid index, and changed the update for the case arr[mid] > target to r = mid - 1 so the search interval strictly shrinks, eliminating the infinite loop.
edgeCasesMissed: Empty input array (n==0) – current code will set r = -1 and the loop terminates correctly, but callers should handle n==0 gracefully.
Very large arrays where indices approach INT_MAX – overflow is now prevented by the safe midpoint calculation.
Target larger than all elements – loop terminates with -1 as expected.
